name: Bank of India
business_summary: Government-owned (73.38%) public-sector bank with a sizeable international franchise (branches and subsidiaries abroad) alongside domestic retail, MSME, agriculture and corporate lending. Market cap Rs62,599cr at P/E 5.0x and P/B 0.66x, dividend yield 3.4%. Q2 FY27 standalone PAT Rs3,202cr (+25% y/y) on strong NII and recoveries; management guides NIM to improve to 2.55% in H2 FY27 after the RBI hike (repo 5.50%). Key issues: NIM sustainability once deposits reprice, treasury sensitivity to yields, ECL transition (April 2027), possible government OFS.

exposures.mechanism: PSU banks: ~60% of loans are repo-linked (EBLR) and reprice immediately (PSBs raised repo-linked lending rates by 25bp on 2026-10-09), deposits reprice slowly; management guides NIM to 2.55% in H2 FY27. +10bp NIM on ~Rs10 lakh cr earning assets = Rs1,000cr pre-tax = Rs750cr post-tax = ~6% of TTM PAT Rs12,517cr; persistence 0.25 => +1.5; P/B 0.66 means re-rating potential from earnings upgrade => +2.5 with wide range because deposit repricing could erase it within 6-12 months.

evidence.note: RBI hiked repo to 5.50%, stance calibrated tightening (The Hindu / SCC Online)

exposures.mechanism: PSU banks hold large G-sec books (~25-28% of assets, AFS ~35%; model est.): AFS ~Rs1 lakh cr x duration 2.5 x 25bp = Rs625cr = ~5% of PAT, persistence 0.25 = -1.3, plus COE/P-B effect => -3. Matches the sign of empirical US10Y -1.23 (t=-1.7).
+3pp credit growth: PSU loan growth currently lags private banks; NII +3.5%, operating leverage => PAT +5%, persistence 0.6 => +3.
PSU banks have structural deposit-share loss; +3pp deposit growth eases CD ratio and funding cost => +1.5.

+50bp credit cost on ~Rs7 lakh cr advances (model est.) = Rs3,500cr pre-tax = Rs2,600cr post-tax = -21% of TTM PAT; persistence 0.5 => -10. At P/B 0.66 and low earnings multiple (P/E 5), the market already discounts a credit cycle, so risk is asymmetric to the downside only if slippages rise.

evidence.note: Q2 PAT +25% to Rs3,202cr on strong NII and recoveries (Business Standard)

exposures.mechanism: BoI unsecured retail is small (~6-8% of loans, model); +1pp delinquency => -0.9% PAT x 0.5; sentiment -1.

ECL framework (effective 2027-04-01, model knowledge) forces day-1 provisioning; Canara fell 6% on a Rs15,000cr warning. BoI GNPA is low but ECL on stage-2 and standard assets applies; transition can be spread over years; -4 and wide band.

evidence.note: Canara fell 6% on Rs15,000cr ECL provision warning (India Infoline)

exposures.mechanism: FIIs 7.6%; PSU banks are a high-beta domestic flow trade; +US$5bn/qtr => +2.
+10% government capex growth boosts PSU infra/wholesale credit demand and fee income; PSU banks have largest infra exposures => PAT +2.5% x 0.6 = +1.5.
+1pp GDP growth lowers slippages and lifts credit growth; PSU beta higher => +3.

BoI runs an overseas book (~15-20% of business; model knowledge): rupee depreciation lifts INR value of foreign income and FX trading gains; but FPI outflow risk offsets. +0.8; empirical USDCNY -2.46 (t=-1.0) insignificant.
1y vol 33%, beta 1.27 to VIX-linked risk-off; empirical coefficient is positive (+0.66, t=1.3), contradictory sign; central -1.5 retained from beta, low confidence.

supply_chain.note: capital support, OFS/dilution risk, dividend policy

supply_chain.note: PSU peers; SBI Q2 PAT +14% aided by exceptional gains (Moneycontrol 2026-11-03)
